2_router_integration.design: New omniengineer_harness.submit_job_auto() -- the single new entry point inside the Omni capability boundary. Runs classify_complexity(task) and dispatches to submit_job() (simple) or submit_job_decomposed() (complex); everything else (authority, ledger, validation) is unchanged, identical to calling the chosen function directly. adapters/omni_engineer_adapter.py::run() and evolution/advance.py::_run_omni_engineer() were changed to call submit_job_auto() instead of submit_job() -- this is the ENTIRE integration change. No new MCP tool, no new router, no new Proposal store, no new queue. studio_router.py, task_router.py's routing logic, and _implementation_router()/_rank_engineering_engines() (Claude Code primary -> Omni Engineer fallback doctrine) are byte-for-byte unchanged.
2_router_integration.proof: tests/test_th3_omni_router_integration.py (new, isolated/synthetic): a TH3-style submit_work payload -> proposal_mod.create() -> advance_one() -> _implementation_router() (claude_code excluded on its own real merits: paid_resources_allowed=False structurally excludes the metered_api claude_code_engineer_v1 candidate before any router logic runs) -> omni_engineer_v1 selected -> submit_job_auto() -> classify_complexity() -> submit_job_decomposed() actually called (spied, not assumed) -> real phase loop runs (inspect/implement/test) -> durable ledger phases + proposal.implementation_job_ids both correctly populated. 11/11 checks pass.

3_complexity_classification.mechanism: omniengineer_harness.classify_complexity(task) -- pure text analysis (stage keywords, distinct file/module mentions, explicit PHASE-N markers, length as a weak signal only in combination with a real structural one). Requires >=2 independent signal categories to fire before returning decomposition_eligible=True -- length alone, or a single stray keyword, is never enough.
3_complexity_classification.calibration: Signal thresholds were calibrated by reading (never running or reusing the content of) historical job 6978adf2 -- confirmed its shape (8511 chars, 5 PHASE-N markers, 6+ stage keywords, multiple named files) clears the >=2-category bar comfortably. A dedicated test constructs a SEPARATE synthetic multi-phase task of similar shape and confirms decomposition_eligible=True; a one-file edit ('Fix the typo in README.md') and a long-but-shapeless task both correctly classify as simple.

6_phase_narrative_accuracy.mechanism: _run_phase() now returns a full attempt_history (every attempt, not just the last), each entry carrying its own model/provider/final_action/summary/commands_executed/files_touched (a diff scoped to THAT attempt alone)/no_progress flag. _record_phase() computes progress_preserved = True whenever ANY attempt in the phase produced a real sandbox diff, regardless of which attempt's final_action reads as success or failure.

6_phase_narrative_accuracy.REAL_LIVE_PROOF: the real bounded-complexity canary (section 10 below) reproduced this EXACT scenario unprompted: the 'implement' phase's first model (qwen3-coder:30b) wrote all 3 real files then hit iteration_ceiling_reached; the second model (qwen3.6:27b) then failed to produce a valid tool call. The phase's final_action correctly reads 'error' -- but progress_preserved=True is recorded, attempts[0].files_touched shows the 3 real files, and the JOB overall still succeeded (promotion_eligible=True) purely because validation.validate() found the real files correct, DESPITE every one of the 3 base phases recording final_action=error. This is the strongest possible live proof of both PHASE_NARRATIVE_ACCURACY and VALIDATION_FIRST simultaneously.
6_phase_narrative_accuracy.FALSE_PHASE_SUCCESS: NO -- no phase in the real canary was ever marked finished/successful on its own say-so; job success came entirely from validation.validate()
